messages:
jana: opening a tiny PR to add 'guardrails' examples for Dedicated capacity onboarding. want a quick sanity-check on SLA tone and label examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789
ai-docs-bot: PR created by jana: docs/pull/789 — reviewers requested: @sam @ops-lee
sam: quick thought — include both a short YAML and a 2-line SDK snippet. readers often copy the YAML straight into infra.
jana: agreed. keeping examples minimal. avoiding the term 'preemption' alone — clarifying reserved-pool semantics instead.
ops-lee: ops note: add text about graceful SLO changes: "under sustained pressure, latency SLOs may degrade; fallback policies are triggered and customers are notified via console/webhook." also mention cooldowns and min_replicas to reduce thrash.
polly: small nit on SLA phrasing: legal wants "targets"/"aims to" rather than absolutes. i'll add a suggested sentence.
sam: sample YAML (tiny):
```
# dedicated/provisioning/example-guardrails.yaml
capacity:
  name: example-tenant-pool
  reserved_gpus: 4
  isolation_labels: ["prod", "eu-west-1"]
  scale_policy:
    target_utilization: 0.7
    cooldown_seconds: 240
    min_replicas: 1
    burst_enabled: false
```
jana: SDK example (v0.8 param names):
```
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
resp = c.create_capacity(name="example-tenant-pool", gpus=4, isolation_labels=["prod","eu-west-1"])
```
ops-lee: add a short bullet describing fallback order: same-region reserved -> cross-region reserved -> hosted cheaper-variant. phrase as "typical ordering" not a guarantee.
polly: also suggest a 1-line callout: "Isolation labels scope routing and placement; use labels to reserve capacity for a single tenant or group."
jana: perfect — i'll push these edits and add a changelog entry. will ping once pushed. thanks :thumbsup:
